title: Grade 11 Mathematics — Conic Sections
description: Circle, parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola — standard forms and properties
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The standard equation of a circle with centre (h,k) and radius r is:
questions.explanation: Standard circle: (x−h)² + (y−k)² = r². Centre (h,k), radius r. General form: x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 with centre (−g,−f) and radius √(g²+f²−c).

questions.question: The parabola y² = 4ax has:
options: Vertex at (0,0), focus at (a,0), opens rightward when a>0
questions.explanation: y² = 4ax: vertex (0,0), focus (a,0), directrix x = −a, axis = x-axis, opens right (a>0) or left (a<0). Length of latus rectum = 4a.

questions.question: The standard form of an ellipse with major axis along x-axis is: (a > b > 0)
questions.explanation: Ellipse: x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 (a > b). Major axis (length 2a) along x-axis, minor axis (length 2b) along y-axis. Foci at (±c, 0) where c² = a² − b².

questions.question: For an ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 (a>b), the eccentricity e satisfies:
questions.explanation: Eccentricity: e = c/a where c² = a² − b². For ellipse: 0 < e < 1. For circle: e = 0. For parabola: e = 1. For hyperbola: e > 1. Eccentricity measures how 'stretched' the conic is.

questions.question: The standard form of a hyperbola with transverse axis along x-axis is:
questions.explanation: Hyperbola: x²/a² − y²/b² = 1. Transverse axis (vertices at ±a on x-axis), conjugate axis (length 2b), asymptotes: y = ±(b/a)x, foci at (±c,0) where c² = a² + b².

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle with centre (2,−3) and radius 5.
For parabola x² = 4ay (upward opening), the focus is at:
questions.explanation: x² = 4ay: opens upward (a>0), vertex (0,0), focus at (0,a), directrix y = −a, axis = y-axis.

questions.question: The length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 is:
questions.explanation: Length of latus rectum of ellipse = 2b²/a. Here a² = 25 → a = 5, b² = 9. LR = 2(9)/5 = 18/5. Options 0 and 3 express the same answer (18/5).

questions.question: The asymptotes of the hyperbola x²/4 − y²/9 = 1 are:
questions.explanation: Asymptotes of x²/a² − y²/b² = 1: y = ±(b/a)x. Here a² = 4, b² = 9 → a = 2, b = 3. Asymptotes: y = ±(3/2)x.

questions.question: The foci of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/7 = 1 are at:
A conic section is formed by intersecting a cone with a plane. A circle is formed when the plane is:
options: Parallel to the axis of the cone
Perpendicular to the axis of the cone
At an angle to one nappe only
Parallel to a generator (element) of the cone
questions.explanation: Circle: plane perpendicular to cone's axis. Ellipse: plane cuts one nappe at an angle. Parabola: plane parallel to one generator. Hyperbola: plane cuts both nappes.

questions.question: For the hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1, the relationship between a, b, c is:
questions.explanation: Hyperbola: c² = a² + b² (c > a > 0). Ellipse: c² = a² − b² (a > c). Difference: in hyperbola c is LARGER than a; in ellipse c is SMALLER than a.

questions.question: The directrix of the parabola y² = 8x is:
The general equation of a circle x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 3 = 0 has centre:
questions.explanation: General form x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0: here 2g = −4 → g = −2, 2f = 6 → f = 3. Centre = (−g, −f) = (2, −3). Radius = √(g²+f²−c) = √(4+9+3) = √16 = 4.

questions.question: The sum of distances from any point on an ellipse to its two foci equals:
questions.explanation: Definition of ellipse: locus of points where sum of distances from two foci = 2a (constant = major axis). At vertex: distance to nearer focus = a − c, to farther = a + c. Sum = 2a. ✓
